executive_summary: On 2020-12-07, observed sessions reached 5,461, representing a 42.0% relative increase compared to the 4-week baseline average of 3,846 sessions. Concurrently, the purchase rate declined by 14.5% in relative terms (a 0.28 percentage point drop from 1.95% to 1.67%), yielding an estimated purchase session gap of 15.5 sessions. Overall, while session acquisition increased substantially, the proportion of sessions resulting in a purchase softened moderately.
why_no_alert: Although the observation satisfied the minimum session threshold (5,461 vs. minimum 150) and met the estimated purchase session gap threshold (15.5 vs. minimum 15), the relative decline in purchase rate of 14.5% fell well short of the required 35% minimum relative rate drop threshold. Because all alerting criteria must be fulfilled simultaneously, the event was classified as 'no_qualifying_anomaly'.
